title: EV Charging Stations Near Me: Map and List
description: Find EV charging stations near any place with EV Charging Stations Near Me — mapped from open data, nearest first. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a market town's map shows the supermarket charger a visiting driver would never have guessed at — the finder's whole value is the ones you did not know.
quick_answer: EV Charging Stations Near Me maps the charging stations OpenStreetMap records around a place you search or your location, ranked nearest first. Search, press find, and browse the stations on the map and list — the layer between 'the car needs charge' and 'there is a plug in that town'.

Moving house with an EV: the neighbourhood's charging map is a moving-in fact as real as the schools.
The nearest charger is a plan; the second nearest is a strategy. The ranked list gives both.
A charger you know is missing tells you the local data's vintage — and OpenStreetMap accepts the correction from anyone.
Nearest first sounds obvious until a river intervenes: the closest plug as the crow flies can be a bridge away by road. The list ranks by distance; your route sense refines it.
Where mappers recorded them, stations carry the practical details. Where they did not, the station still appears — presence first, particulars where the data has them.

popular_table.note: OpenStreetMap charging data is community-built: strong in much of Europe and North America's cities, thinner in rural areas — improving with every mapper who adds a plug.

faq: Does it show connector types and prices?

Where the map data records them, the detail travels with the station; prices and live status belong to operators and change faster than maps. Treat this as the where, and the operator as the how much.
How current is the data?
As current as the last mapper's edit in that area — days in active cities, longer in quiet ones. A station you find missing can be added to OpenStreetMap by anyone, including you.
Can I use the tool without sharing my precise location?
Yes — search a place name instead. Location is one input option, never a requirement.
Why might a boundary or place name look different elsewhere?
Place data varies by source and date; charging operators' own maps draw from their networks rather than the open record.
Does MapBench store my browser location?
No — it is used for the search and not kept.
The nearest station is across a river or border.
Distance ranking is geographic. Your route may prefer the second entry; the list gives you the order to judge from.
Tesla-only stations included?
Stations are listed as the data records them, including network restrictions where tagged. The car's compatibility is a filter you apply with the record in hand.
Can I plan a full route's charging here?
This finds stations near a point; chain points along your route for the whole journey — the range ring from EV Range Radius frames each hop.
A charger exists but is not listed.
It is unmapped or was mapped after the data snapshot. OpenStreetMap edits flow in — and local knowledge like yours is precisely how the map learns.
Fast chargers specifically?
Where the data tags power and connector detail, the station record shows it. Dedicated network apps filter harder; this map's job is the unbiased where.
Free charging points?
Pricing lives with operators and changes often — the station's own listing or app is the source. The map's neutrality is why it shows all networks alike.
